codeReview.summary: All 6 scrutiny fixes from the foundation review were correctly addressed. The diff is clean, focused, and net-negative in lines (42 added, 62 removed). Each fix is well-scoped: (1) ResearchSection now shows prior data at opacity-50 during rerun instead of a skeleton overlay, matching the pattern used by ContactsSection and ScoringSection. (2) DEFAULT_WEIGHTS extracted to lib/utils/scoring.ts with both consumers importing from there. (3) findContactsByCompanyId() added to contacts-repo.ts and used by both briefs.ts and the orchestration route, eliminating direct DB queries. (4) Silent catch in BriefRunController replaced with a toast.error() with user-friendly messaging. (5) Unused companyId prop removed from OutreachSection. (6) OutreachSection given a key prop tied to dataVersion so it remounts when data updates, fixing stale contactStates. Cross-area flow verification was done via agent-browser with comprehensive interactive checks. TypeScript and ESLint both pass cleanly.

issues.description: ResearchSection adds `pointer-events-none` alongside `opacity-50` during rerun, while ContactsSection (line 183) and ScoringSection (line 309) only use `opacity-50`. This is a minor pattern inconsistency — the visual effect is correct, but the interaction model differs slightly across sections. pointer-events-none is arguably the better pattern (prevents user interaction with stale data during refresh), but it should ideally be applied consistently to all sections.

The condition `(state === 'running' && reportData) && reportData` has a redundant `&& reportData` check — the outer condition already checks `reportData` is truthy. This is cosmetically redundant but functionally correct.
ResearchSection adds `pointer-events-none` alongside `opacity-50` during rerun, while ContactsSection and ScoringSection only use `opacity-50`. Minor pattern inconsistency across sections.
Redundant `&& reportData` check in the combined render condition — the outer disjunction already verifies `reportData` is truthy for the running case.

The discovered issue about outreach section scores using DEFAULT_WEIGHTS while scoring section uses scoringConfig.weights (when configured) is a real divergence risk. If a user sets custom weights in scoring config, the outreach section's ranked order may differ from the scoring section. Consider passing scoringConfig weights through to getBriefData's recommendation calculation.
